title: Azerbaijani plov (saffron rice with a lavash crust)

ingredients.name: saffron threads, steeped in 3 tbsp hot water
salt for the cooking water, plus more to taste

steps: Rinse the rice several times until the water runs clear, then soak in salted water for 30 minutes.
Boil a large pot of salted water and cook the drained rice for about 6 to 8 minutes until it is just tender outside but still firm in the middle. Drain.
Mix half of the melted butter with the saffron liquid and a spoonful of the rice to make a golden portion.
Brush the base of a heavy pot with butter and line it with the lavash. Pile in the rice in a cone, make a few holes with a spoon handle, and drizzle with the remaining butter.
Cover tightly with a towel under the lid and steam over very low heat for 30 to 40 minutes until the rice is fluffy and the bread has crisped into a golden base.
Spoon the saffron rice over the top and serve with sabzi qovurma or another stew.

title: Badambura (Azerbaijani almond pastry)
steps: Mix the yeast into the warm milk, then work the butter into the flour. Add the egg yolks and milk and knead into a smooth dough. Rest for 45 minutes.
Combine the ground almonds, sugar and cardamom for the filling.
Roll out the dough thinly and cut into diamonds or squares of about 7 cm.
Put a spoonful of filling in the centre of each, fold the dough over into a triangle or diamond shape and press the edges tightly closed.
Bake at 170 C (340 F) for 20 to 25 minutes until just golden, keeping the colour pale.
Cool, then dust with powdered sugar before serving.

title: Badimcan dolmasi (Azerbaijani stuffed aubergines and peppers)

ingredients.name: tomatoes, tops cut off and scooped out
salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Cut the stems from the aubergines and slice a lengthwise pocket in each, scooping out some flesh and reserving it. Salt them lightly, rest for 15 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Fry the onion in 1 tablespoon of oil until soft, add the lamb and the chopped aubergine flesh and cook for 8 minutes. Stir in the chickpeas, herbs, salt and pepper.
Stuff the aubergines, peppers and tomatoes with the filling and set them snugly in a wide pot or baking dish.
Dilute the tomato paste in the hot water with remaining oil and pour around the vegetables.
Cover and simmer on low heat, or bake at 180 C (350 F), for 45 to 50 minutes until the vegetables are very soft.
Serve warm with yogurt and flatbread.

title: Bozbash (Azerbaijani lamb, chickpea and potato stew)

ingredients.name: lamb on the bone, cut into chunks
dried sour plums or 3 tbsp tamarind-free sour plum paste (or lemon juice, to taste)
salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Put the lamb and drained chickpeas in a pot with the water, bring to a boil and skim the foam.
Add the onion and turmeric, cover and simmer on low heat for about 1.5 hours until the lamb and chickpeas are nearly tender.
Add the tomatoes and potatoes along with the dried plums, salt and pepper, and simmer for 30 more minutes until the potatoes are cooked through.
Taste for sourness and salt. The broth should be golden, fairly brothy and gently tart.
Serve in deep bowls, with fresh herbs and flatbread at the side.

title: Doghramaj (Azerbaijani cold yogurt and vegetable soup)
steps: Whisk the yogurt with the cold water until smooth and pourable, then stir in the garlic and salt.
Combine the cucumbers, radishes, spring onions, herbs and eggs in a large bowl.
Pour the yogurt mixture over the vegetables and stir gently.
Chill for at least 30 minutes so the flavours blend.
Serve very cold in bowls with extra herbs on top, and flatbread at the side.

title: Dushbara (tiny Azerbaijani lamb dumplings in broth)

ingredients.name: dried mint, plus extra to serve
garlic, crushed and mixed with 2 tbsp vinegar
salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Knead the flour, egg, water and a pinch of salt into a stiff dough, cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Mix the lamb with the grated onion, salt, pepper and half of the mint for the filling.
Roll the dough very thin and cut it into squares about 3 cm wide.
Place a little filling (about the size of a hazelnut) on each square and pinch the corners together to make small closed dumplings.
Bring the stock to a boil, add the dumplings and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until they float and the filling is cooked through.
Ladle into bowls and serve with the garlic-vinegar mixture and a sprinkle of dried mint.

title: Levengi (walnut and sour plum stuffed baked chicken)

ingredients.name: dried sour plums or sour cherries, chopped
salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Cook the onions in 2 tablespoons of butter until golden, then let them cool.
Mix the onions with the walnuts, dried plums, pomegranate molasses, half of the turmeric, salt and pepper into a coarse, moist stuffing.
Rub the chicken inside and out with salt, pepper and the remaining turmeric.
Fill the cavity loosely with the stuffing and close the opening with toothpicks or kitchen twine.
Place in a roasting tin, dot with the remaining butter and roast at 190 C (375 F) for about 1 hour 15 minutes, basting now and then, until the skin is golden and the juices run clear.
Rest for 10 minutes, then carve and serve with the stuffing, rice, and more pomegranate syrup at the table.

title: Lula kebab (Azerbaijani minced lamb skewers)

ingredients.name: ground sumac, plus extra to serve

steps: Mix the lamb, grated onion, salt, pepper and sumac and knead the mixture for several minutes until it turns sticky and holds together.
Cover and chill for at least 1 hour so it firms up.
Wet your hands and shape portions of the mixture into long, thick sausages around flat metal skewers, pressing firmly so they grip.
Grill over hot charcoal or under a very hot grill for 8 to 10 minutes, turning often, until browned outside and cooked through.
Slide the kebabs off onto flatbread, scatter with red onion and sumac and serve at once.

title: Pakhlava (Azerbaijani walnut and saffron layered pastry)

ingredients.name: egg yolk mixed with a pinch of saffron, for brushing

steps: Knead the flour, egg, sour cream and half of the butter into a soft dough, then rest for 1 hour.
Mix the ground nuts, 200 g of sugar and the cardamom for the filling.
Divide the dough into 6 pieces and roll the first as thinly as you can, laying it in a buttered rectangular tin. Brush with butter and repeat for 2 more sheets, then spread over half of the filling.
Roll and layer 2 more sheets with butter between them, add the remaining filling, then finish with the last dough sheet.
Cut the pastry into diamonds before baking, brush the top with the saffron yolk and bake at 180 C (350 F) for 40 to 45 minutes until golden.
Meanwhile simmer the 250 g sugar, water and lemon juice for 10 minutes. Pour the cooled syrup over the warm pakhlava and leave it to soak for a few hours.

title: Piti (Azerbaijani lamb and chickpea stew)

ingredients.name: lamb shoulder or neck on the bone, cut into pieces
dried sour plums or dried apricots
saffron threads, steeped in 3 tbsp hot water
salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Put the lamb, drained chickpeas and half of the onions in a large pot with the water. Bring to a boil, skim the foam and simmer, covered, for 1 hour.
Add the potatoes, tomatoes, dried plums, the remaining onion, salt and pepper, then simmer for another 30 to 40 minutes until the chickpeas and meat are tender.
Stir in the saffron and its liquid and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Traditionally the dish is baked in individual clay crocks; you can ladle it into ovenproof bowls and bake at 180 C (350 F) for 15 minutes, or serve straight from the pot.
Break flatbread into bowls and ladle the broth over it, then serve the meat and vegetables alongside, sprinkled with dried mint.

title: Qutab (thin folded flatbreads with lamb and onion)
steps: Knead the flour, water and salt into a smooth, firm dough, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the lamb with the onions, sumac, pepper and salt for the filling. Keep it raw; it cooks inside the dough.
Divide the dough into 12 balls and roll each into a very thin round about 20 cm across.
Spread a thin layer of filling over one half of each circle, fold the other half over and press the edges together to seal.
Heat a dry, wide frying pan or flat griddle over medium heat and cook each qutab for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until brown spots appear and the meat is cooked through.
Brush the hot qutabs with melted butter and serve at once, with yogurt and a little extra sumac.

title: Qutab with greens (herb-filled flatbreads)

ingredients.name: butter, plus extra melted butter for brushing

steps: Make the dough from the flour, water and salt, knead until smooth and rest it under a cloth for 30 minutes.
Wilt the spinach in 2 tablespoons of butter for 2 minutes, then let it cool and squeeze out any excess liquid.
Mix the spinach with the herbs, spring onions, sumac and salt to make the filling.
Roll the dough into 12 very thin rounds, put filling on one half of each, fold over and seal the edges.
Cook the pastries on a dry hot pan for 2 minutes per side until lightly spotted and crisp at the edges.
Brush with melted butter and serve hot with plain yogurt.

title: Sabzi qovurma (Azerbaijani lamb and fresh herb stew)

ingredients.name: mixed fresh herbs (parsley, cilantro, dill, spinach), chopped
lemon, juiced (or a splash of verjuice)
salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Brown the lamb in the butter in a heavy pot, then add the onions and fry until golden.
Stir in the turmeric, salt and pepper, add the hot water and simmer, covered, for about 1 hour until the lamb is tender.
Add the herbs and dried plums and cook, uncovered, for 15 to 20 minutes until the herbs are very soft and the sauce is thick and dark green.
Add lemon juice or verjuice to taste for a gentle sourness.
Serve with plain rice or plov and a bowl of garlicky yogurt.

title: Shekerbura (almond-filled Novruz pastries)
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the warm milk, then rub the butter into the flour, add the egg and the milk mixture and knead into a soft, smooth dough. Rest for 1 hour.
Mix the ground nuts with the sugar and cardamom for the filling.
Roll the dough out thinly and cut into rounds about 8 cm wide.
Put a spoonful of filling on each round, fold into a half-moon and press the edges closed. Use a fork or the tip of a knife to make a pattern along the curved side.
Place on a lined tray, brush with egg yolk and bake at 180 C (350 F) for 20 to 25 minutes until pale gold.
Cool completely before serving, with tea.

title: Shorgoghal (spiced savoury Novruz pastries)

ingredients.name: egg yolk mixed with a pinch of saffron or turmeric

steps: Mix the flour, yeast and half the salt, rub in the cold butter, add the milk and knead into a smooth dough. Rest for 1 hour.
Warm the melted butter with the cumin, aniseed, cinnamon, pepper and remaining salt for 2 to 3 minutes to make a fragrant spiced butter, then cool it.
Roll the dough into a thin rectangle, brush it with some of the spiced butter, roll it up like a log and cut into 12 slices.
Flatten each slice into a round with a rolling pin, put a small spoonful of the remaining spiced butter in the centre and pinch the edges up around it, then flatten lightly.
Place on a lined tray, brush with the saffron yolk and sprinkle with poppy seeds.
Bake at 180 C (350 F) for 20 to 25 minutes until golden. Serve warm or at room temperature with tea.

title: Yarpaq dolmasi (Azerbaijani stuffed grape leaves)

ingredients.name: salt and black pepper to taste

steps: If using fresh leaves, blanch them in hot water for 1 minute; if brined, soak and rinse well. Trim the stems.
Mix the lamb, rice, onion, herbs, dried mint, salt and pepper thoroughly.
Place a leaf shiny-side down, put a teaspoon of filling near the stem end, fold in the sides and roll up tightly into a small cylinder. Repeat with the rest.
Line the base of a pot with a few spare leaves, pack the dolmas in tight rows and dot with butter.
Add the hot water, set a small plate on top to keep them from unrolling, cover and simmer for 45 minutes until the rice and lamb are cooked.
Serve warm with garlicky yogurt.
